paragraphs.title: The King Discovers That Mordecai Was Not Rewarded

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “could not the king sleep.”
easy.q: What happened to the king’s sleep that night?

answers: The book of records of the chronicles
easy.explanation: The king commanded that “the book of records of the chronicles” be brought.
easy.q: What book did the king command to be brought?

answers: They sought to lay hand on the king
easy.explanation: Mordecai had told that Bigthana and Teresh sought to lay hand on King Ahasuerus.
easy.q: What did Mordecai tell about Bigthana and Teresh?

medium.explanation: Because the king could not sleep, he commanded the records to be read.
medium.q: Why did the king have the records read before him?

answers: The king was unable to sleep
The king chose to sleep later
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the king was unable to sleep.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “could not the king sleep” mean?

answers: Mordecai had received nothing for his deed
Mordecai had become a royal servant
medium.explanation: The servants answered, “There is nothing done for him.”
medium.q: What did the king learn about Mordecai’s reward?

answers: The king’s sleeplessness led to the records being read and Mordecai’s deed being discovered
Haman’s arrival caused the king to forget Mordecai
The reading of the records caused Bigthana and Teresh to rebel
challenge.explanation: The king could not sleep, the records were read, and Mordecai’s unrewarded deed was discovered.
challenge.q: What chain of events is described in these verses?

answers: He exposed a plot against the king
He prepared a banquet for the king
challenge.explanation: Mordecai had reported that Bigthana and Teresh sought to lay hand on the king.
challenge.q: What was the importance of Mordecai’s report?

answers: What honour and dignity hath been done to Mordecai for this?
challenge.explanation: The king asked what honor and dignity had been done to Mordecai, but learned that nothing had been done for him.
challenge.q: Which question shows that the king expected Mordecai to have received honor?

answers: To ask that Mordecai be hanged
To invite the king to a banquet
easy.explanation: Haman came to speak to the king “to hang Mordecai on the gallows.”
easy.q: Why had Haman come to the king’s outer court?

easy.explanation: The servants said, “Behold, Haman standeth in the court.”
easy.q: Whom did the king’s servants say was standing in the court?

easy.explanation: Haman thought in his heart, “To whom would the king delight to do honour more than to myself?”
easy.q: Who thought that the king wanted to honor him more than anyone else?

answers: What should be done to the man whom the king wished to honor
medium.explanation: The king asked, “What shall be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour?”
medium.q: What did the king ask Haman?

answers: To seat him at the king’s gate
To dress him in royal apparel and place him on the king’s horse
To invite him to Esther’s banquet
medium.explanation: Haman proposed royal apparel, the king’s horse, the royal crown, and a public proclamation.
medium.q: What honor did Haman propose for the man?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that the king wishes to honor the man.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “delighteth to honour” mean?

answers: Haman personally wanted to honor Mordecai
The king commanded Haman to do exactly what he had proposed for Mordecai
The king’s servants confused Haman with Mordecai
challenge.explanation: The king ordered Haman to take the apparel and horse and do so to Mordecai the Jew.
challenge.q: Why did Haman’s proposal become the honor given to Mordecai?

answers: He was standing in the court
He was commanded to take the apparel and horse and lead Mordecai through the city
challenge.explanation: The king commanded Haman to take the apparel and horse and carry out the ceremony.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Haman had to perform the honor ceremony himself?

answers: The king remembered Mordecai’s service and his lack of reward
The king did not know who Mordecai was
The king wanted to destroy the royal records
challenge.explanation: After hearing that nothing had been done for Mordecai, the king ordered him to be honored.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the king’s command to honor Mordecai?

paragraphs.title: Haman’s Humiliation and Summons to the Banquet

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Mordecai came again to the king’s gate.”
easy.q: Where did Mordecai return after being honored?

answers: Mourning and with his head covered
easy.explanation: Haman went home “mourning, and having his head covered.”
The king’s chamberlains came and hurried to bring Haman to the banquet.
easy.q: Who hurried to bring Haman to Esther’s banquet?

answers: Everything that had happened to him
medium.explanation: The KJV says that Haman told them “every thing that had befallen him.”
medium.q: What did Haman tell Zeresh and all his friends?

medium.explanation: These words describe Haman’s sorrow and humiliation after honoring Mordecai.
medium.q: What does “mourning, and having his head covered” show about Haman’s condition?

answers: Mordecai had nothing to do with the matter
Haman had begun to fall before him
medium.explanation: They said, “before whom thou hast begun to fall.”
medium.q: What did Zeresh and the wise men say about Mordecai?

answers: He went from planning Mordecai’s death, to honoring him, to being humiliated
He went from being a banquet guest to becoming king
He went from honoring Mordecai to receiving honor from him
challenge.explanation: Haman came intending to hang Mordecai, was forced to honor him, and then went home mourning.
challenge.q: What change in Haman’s position is shown in these verses?

answers: They announce that Haman’s situation is beginning to turn against him
They explain how to read the royal records
They command Mordecai to attend the banquet
challenge.explanation: They warn Haman that he has begun to fall before Mordecai the Jew and will not prevail against him.
challenge.q: Why are Zeresh’s and the wise men’s words important?

answers: The king’s chamberlains hurry to bring Haman to the banquet
challenge.explanation: While they were still talking, the king’s chamberlains came and hurried Haman to Esther’s banquet.
challenge.q: What creates urgency at the end of the passage?
